verdict.reasoning: Patient reports diarrhea for three days with central lower abdominal pain and vomiting this morning: 'it's lasting for like three days... I have a bit of abdominal pain and I had a bit of vomiting' and later confirms last vomit was this morning.
Patient describes very frequent urges to defecate: 'I go to a toilet and then when I finish, I need to. I feel I need to go again' and 'I just go into the toilet every 10 minutes.'
Sensation of incomplete evacuation is implied by: 'I go to a toilet and then when I finish, I need to. I feel I need to go again.'
Patient denies blood in stools: 'Have you noticed any blood?' / 'No, I haven't noticed any blood.' (in context of diarrhea).

Location and nature of pain: 'the pain is mainly focused in the center area of the abdomen, like under the belly button. And sometimes I can hear my stomach, like the cramps.' Mild tenderness with pressure: 'when you press on your tummy, does it cause any pain? ... Oh, it does a little bit.'
Pain relief with bowel movements/passing gas is supported: 'it seems to be alleviate the toilet and maybe it's like gas.'
Patient reports nausea: 'then I got a bit of nausea and I vomited.'
Single vomiting episode after fruit this morning: 'I think it was this morning... I had some fruit... Then I got a bit of nausea and I vomited. And then. Yeah, that was it.'

Patient clarifies no blood in vomit, red color from strawberries: 'Did you notice any blood when you vomit?' / initially unsure, then 'I'm sorry. I don't think there is blood because... it was strawberries that I was having for breakfast. So. Yeah, it wasn't blood.'

Decreased intake and likely under-hydration: 'I try not to eat a lot because I just go into the toilet every 10 minutes' and 'Maybe I'm not drinking enough water... I think I don't drink enough water.'

Denies clear fever but mentions sweating and uncertainty about low-grade fever: 'I didn't have any fever recently. I was sweating a little bit last for bed, but I. Not sure if I had a bit of fever, but very little, but I don't think so.'
History of asthma and inhaler use: 'So I have. I have. I have asthma and I take some. Some inhaler.'

No change in baseline shortness of breath: 'have you noticed any problems with your breathing?' / 'I always have problems with my breathing because of the asthma... but a part of the normal. I haven't, I haven't.'
Denies chest pain: 'And how about chest? Have you noticed any chest pain?' / 'No, I haven't. I haven't noticed any chest pain.'
Impact on work: 'I can't go to work because I need to go like every... I need to be like, close to the toilet.' and 'so I'm spending some time at home.'
Past medical history of asthma: 'So I have. I have. I have asthma.'
Current inhaler use: 'I take some. Some inhaler.' and 'When I get a bit of anxiety, I. I use my inhaler.'
Brand change because prior inhaler ran out: 'my inhaler kind of run out. The one. Because, you know, I'm a foreigner, so I have this brand, but I bought a new one here.'
Patient states NKDA: 'I have an allergy. I have nkda allergy.' (interpreted as no known drug allergies).
Family history: 'my father, because he died about 10 years ago of cancer.'
Work and staying home: 'I can't go to work because I need to go like every... I need to be like, close to the toilet.' and 'so I'm spending some time at home.'

Doctor diagnoses gastroenteritis/food-related infection matching described course: 'what it sounds like to me is that you might have eaten something bad... This is normally called gastroenteritis' and symptoms are 'three days' diarrhea, central cramps, one vomiting episode, no blood, not getting better or worse.

Risk of dehydration inferred from high stool frequency and low intake; doctor emphasizes fluids: 'you're losing lots at the moment' and advises 'drink lots of water and fluids,' consistent with concern for dehydration.

Asthma stable, no acute exacerbation despite inhaler change: patient reports usual breathing problems only, 'a part of the normal. I haven't,' and no respiratory red flags are elicited; inhaler brand change noted without new respiratory symptoms.

Patient expresses health anxiety due to father’s cancer: 'I always have in the back of my head, my father, because he died... of cancer... this is kind of the. My worries.' Doctor reassures: 'most suggestive of an infection of your tummy and less likely to be something your father had.'
Advice to increase fluids: 'Number one is to drink lots of water and fluids because you're losing lots at the moment.'
Advice to monitor for fevers: 'Number two is to make sure and look out for any fevers. So if you start getting a temperature, then you need...' (implied monitoring).
Stay home until improving: 'Three is stay home for the time being until you get slightly better.'
Antibiotics to be avoided: 'Normally things like antibiotics don't help. They make the situation worse.'

Contingency for GP review: 'If you feel you're getting much worse, then I would suggest you go and see your GP in real life in person so they can look at your belly.' and patient agrees to 'wait a couple of days... and then I will book.' This supports review if not improving over 1–2 days.

Asthma plan content: doctor states inhaler unlikely cause: 'It's very unlikely for an inhaler to cause tummy pain like this.' No respiratory red flags are noted, and patient reports no worsening breathing or chest pain, indicating stable asthma with no concerning respiratory features.
